title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the 1975–76 handwritten notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. It is a typed page, numbered '-94- IX', from the typescript of SGA 7, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §7, on abelian parts and pairings. The neighbouring pages are handwritten homological computations with the truncation functors τ_N and φ_N. Those computations have nothing to do with this page, so the sheet was most likely reused as scrap paper or misfiled.

The mathematics, in modern terms:

(1) End of the proof of a perfectness statement over a more general base S. Take abelian schemes B and B' (the abelian parts) and a G_m-biextension W^{ab} of (B, B'). It is a perfect duality, meaning it identifies B' with the dual abelian scheme B^∨, as soon as it is perfect over a dense open U (where the original abelian schemes have good reduction). This is checked fibrewise at the points η of U. By the usual localisation argument, one reduces to the case where S is a trait with generic point η, which was treated earlier.

(2) The orthogonality relation says the toric parts of A^o and A'^o are orthogonal for the pairing W. It lets one extend formulas (5.5.7)–(5.5.9) and Theorem 5.6 to this context, with 'restriction to the generic point' replaced by 'restriction to U'. Theorem 5.6 is the comparison of the monodromy pairing and the component groups with the duality.

(3) Proposition 7.5. Let S be a complete trait with fraction field K, and A_K an abelian variety with semi-stable reduction. Let A be its Néron model and A^o the neutral component. Over each S_n = Spec(R/m^{n+1}), the group A^o_n is an extension of an abelian scheme B_n by a torus. The B_n form a formal abelian scheme, which is algebraised (procedure of 7.1) into an abelian scheme B = A^{ab} over S, functorial in A_K.

Now let W_K be a divisorial correspondence, i.e. a G_m-biextension, on (A_K, A'_K), and let W be its canonical extension (1.4) to (A^o, A'^o). The reductions W_n descend uniquely to biextensions W^{ab}_n of (B_n, B'_n), because the tori are orthogonal. These algebraise to a unique divisorial correspondence W^{ab} on (A^{ab}, A'^{ab}), whose pullback to (A^o_n, A'^o_n) is W_n for every n.

The purpose of all this is the theory of semi-stable degeneration: the abelian part of the Néron model and the behaviour of duality and pairings under reduction. It is the preparation for the monodromy pairing and Grothendieck's orthogonality theorem.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible. The general-S perfectness step is only sketched ('l'argument habituel'), as it is in the published text.

ideas.what: Abelian part B = A^{ab} of the neutral component of a semi-stable Néron model over a complete trait, obtained by algebraising the abelian quotients of the infinitesimal reductions
ideas.modern_name: abelian part of a semi-abelian Néron model (formal → algebraic via Grothendieck existence)

ideas.what: Descent of the canonically extended biextension W to a biextension W^{ab} of the abelian parts, using orthogonality of the toric parts
ideas.modern_name: induced pairing / biextension on abelian parts; orthogonality theorem

ideas.what: Perfectness of W^{ab} checked on a dense open U, reduced to the trait case
ideas.modern_name: duality of abelian parts (B' ≅ B^∨) for semi-stable degenerations

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX (Prop. 7.5), probably reused as scrap paper inside the 1976 divided-power de Rham notes. Its content is well known and credited to Grothendieck. The only point of interest is archival: its physical presence in this folder.
transcription_corrections: Header: this is SGA 7 Exp. IX, typed page 94; it is not part of the handwritten de Rham notes.
'en tout point η de U[?]' should read 'de U'.
'S est un trait[?]' — the smudged word is 'trait'.
'modèle de Néron A, de A_K' is 'modèle de Néron A de A_K' (the comma is a typing artifact); 'le procédé de 7.1' carries a handwritten correction of the number.
